terms.definition: To play with a more forceful accent or emphasis.

terms.definition: An embellishment that indicates to decorate a note with its upper and lower neighbor, in that order. (The opposite order would be an "inverted" turn.) For example, a turn on C would be performed C–D–C–B–C. This embellishment is a specific kind of double neighbor.
terms.example: The turn adds elegance to the phrase.

terms.definition: An embellishing tone often occurring on a strong beat that is approached by leap and left by step in the opposite direction.
terms.example: The appoggiatura creates tension before resolution.

terms.definition: A symbol placed on the left side of a staff that indicates which notes are assigned to different lines and spaces.

terms.definition: As an "F" clef, the bass clef shows which line of the staff is F₃ by surrounding it with two dots.
terms.example: Bass and cello parts use the bass clef.

terms.definition: An indication of meter in Western music notation, often made up of two numbers stacked vertically.
terms.example: 4/4 time means four quarter notes per measure.

terms.definition: In music notation, a collection of sharps or flats written at the beginning of each line (immediately after the clef) to signal that certain notes are always sharp/flat.
terms.example: Three sharps indicate the key of A major.

terms.definition: Raises a note by a half step.

terms.definition: Lowers a note by a half step.
terms.example: B flat is one semitone lower than B.

terms.definition: Neither sharp nor flat.
terms.example: The natural sign cancels the previous sharp.

terms.definition: Connects two or more notes of the same pitch; notes after the initial one are not rearticulated.

terms.definition: A curved line placed over notes to indicate that they should be played or sung without separation.

terms.definition: Created by bar lines, a measure (or bar) is equivalent to one beat grouping.

terms.definition: Vertical lines that create measures.

terms.definition: Indicates one should repeat either the previous measure, or the previous two measures.

terms.definition: A vertical sonority.

terms.definition: A type of homophony in which one can clearly distinguish between melodic and supporting voices, usually with differing rhythms between them.

terms.definition: The duration of musical sounds and rests in time.

terms.definition: A pulse in music to which one can tap or clap along. A grouped hierarchy of beats forms a meter.

terms.definition: How fast or slow a work is performed; many tempo markings are in Italian or another non-English language.

terms.definition: A recurring pattern of accents that occur over time. Meters are indicated in music notation with a time signature.

terms.definition: Beat 1 of a measure, which is conducted with a downward motion.

terms.definition: The last beat of a measure which is conducted with an upward motion.
terms.example: The upbeat prepares the next measure.

terms.definition: A rhythmic phenomenon in which the hierarchy of the underlying meter is contradicted through surface rhythms. Syncopation is usually created through accents and/or longer durations.

terms.definition: A melodic and harmonic goal. In classical tonal music, cadence types include Perfect Authentic (PAC), Imperfect Authentic (IAC), and Half (HC).

terms.definition: A relatively complete musical thought that exhibits trajectory toward a goal (often a cadence).
terms.example: Each phrase should be shaped expressively.

terms.definition: In strict four-voice writing: 1) Approach the chordal seventh by step or common tone 2) Resolve the chordal seventh down by step Reminder: the chordal seventh is different from the leading tone.

terms.definition: Used after tempo alterations, such as ritardando or accelerando. Indicates a return to the original tempo.

terms.definition: The act of moving pitch content by a certain interval.

terms.definition: A change of key.

terms.definition: As an acoustic phenomenon, frequencies vibrating at whole-number ratios with one another; as a cultural phenomenon, perceived stability in a chord or interval.

terms.definition: A perceived quality of auditory roughness in an interval or chord.
terms.example: The dissonance creates tension before resolution.

A complex large-scale musical form that can be understood as an elaborate version of rounded binary form with a balanced component. The larger level names are as follows: Exposition (≈A), Development (≈B), and Recapitulation (≈A′). The secondary theme is presented in a non-tonic key in the exposition, and crucially, it is restated in the recapitulation in the tonic key. The exposition and recapitulation often end with a large suffix (closing section).
